INTEGRATED SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

6. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.

8. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

10. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

11. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

12. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.

16. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
